title: Search-Based LLMs for Code Optimization
technique_name: SBLLM (execution-based representative sample selection + adaptive optimization pattern retrieval + genetic operator-inspired CoT prompting, evolutionary loop)
core_idea_checked: Iteratively evolves candidate optimizations by selecting representative executed samples, retrieving optimization patterns and applying genetic-operator-style CoT prompts to combine them.
gain_metric: SP@5 speedup rate (%) on Python, GPT-4
gain_note: Columns are Instruction, ICL, RAG, COT, SBLLM; GPT-4 on 10% test sample; top-5 selection. Edits human-written slow programs (PIE).
effect_correctness_headline: baseline methods generate at least 27.18% incorrect code for Python. In contrast, SBLLM reduces this rate by 17.18% (ChatGPT top-1)
benchmarks: PIE (from CodeNet): Python test 986, C++ test 994; GPT-4 run on a 10% random sample of the test set
models: CodeLlama-34b-Instruct (open, code-specialized instruct); Gemini-pro (closed); gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 (closed instruct); gpt-4-1106-preview (closed instruct)
authors: Shu-Zheng Gao; Cui-Yun Gao; Wenchao Gu; M. Lyu
venue: International Conference on Software Engineering; arXiv

title: PerfCodeGen: Improving Performance of LLM Generated Code with Execution Feedback
technique_name: PerfCodeGen (correctness refinement with reflection/planning + performance refinement using most time-consuming unit test feedback)
core_idea_checked: After correctness refinement, executes candidate code on unit tests, reports the slowest test and its time, and asks the LLM to optimize accordingly.
gain_note: Printed delta (+13.14) does not match difference (13.04); vs base model, not strongest refinement baseline; tests used as both feedback and evaluation.
benchmarks: HumanEval (164); MBPP sanitized test (257); APPS test sanitized (3,249)
models: Phi-3-mini 3.8B open instruct; Llama 3 8B open instruct; Mixtral 8x7B open instruct; Command R 35B open instruct; Llama 3 70B open instruct; GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 closed; GPT-4-0613 closed
authors: Yun Peng; Akhilesh Deepak Gotmare; M. Lyu; Caiming Xiong; S. Savarese; Doyen Sahoo
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM Second International Conference on AI Foundation Models and Software Engineering (Forge); arXiv

title: PromSec: Prompt Optimization for Secure Generation of Functional Source Code with Large Language Models (LLMs)
technique_name: PromSec (gGAN-guided iterative prompt optimization)
core_idea_checked: A graph GAN trained with a contrastive loss repairs vulnerable code graphs, and the repaired code is turned into an improved prompt for the LLM in an iterative loop.
gain_metric: number of CWEs per code base (Bandit/SpotBugs)
baseline_name: BL1: Pearce et al. prompt templates with security-tool context
gain_note: Security results only in figures/histograms (Fig. 6, 8); no printed baseline/technique CWE numbers; headline gains are in cost (order-of-magnitude fewer queries).
effect_correctness_headline: FT passes Overall (20 code bases): PromSec 20, BL1 11, BL2 5
benchmarks: Python code bases from Pearce et al. (MITRE, CodeQL docs, hand-crafted): 500 training graphs, 100 test code bases; Java prompts from AixBench/CoderEval: 200 train, 100 test
models: GPT-3.5 Turbo (closed, default); Bard (closed, transfer); CodeLlama-13B-Instruct (open, code-specialized, transfer)
authors: Mahmoud Nazzal; Issa Khalil; Abdallah Khreishah; Nhathai Phan
venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security; arXiv

title: Transformer-based Vulnerability Detection in Code at EditTime: Zero-shot, Few-shot, or Fine-tuning?
technique_name: DeepDevVuln filtering of LLM completions (fine-tuned CodeBERT vulnerability detector)
core_idea_checked: A fine-tuned transformer vulnerability detector flags vulnerable patterns in incomplete code at edit time; applied to filter vulnerable LLM completions.
gain_metric: Vulnerability reduction rate (share of scenarios with a CodeQL-flagged completion)
gain_note: Relative figure: 89.74% reduction for text-davinci-003 (21 of 27 = 78.00% vulnerable scenarios -> 2 of 24 = 8.0%); valid scenario count also drops after filtering. Technique value = 100 - 89.74.
benchmarks: Pearce et al. scenarios: 29 Python plus 11 new JavaScript scenarios (40 total); 25 completions per scenario
models: CodeGen (2B/6B, open, code); code-cushman-001 (closed, code); code-davinci-002 (closed, code); text-davinci-003 (closed, instruct)
note: Main contribution is an edit-time vulnerability detector; use on LLM completions is a filtering application.
authors: Chan, Aaron; Anant Kharkar; Roshanak Zilouchian Moghaddam; Yevhen Mohylevskyy; Alec Helyar; Eslam Kamal
venue: arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University); arXiv.org

title: Franc: A Lightweight Framework for High-Quality Code Generation
technique_name: FRANC repair via generated knowledge prompting with static analyzer messages (P1/P2/P3)
core_idea_checked: Builds a repair prompt from the static analyzer message (generated-knowledge prompting, three structures) and re-queries the LLM to fix quality issues.
gain_metric: % prompts with at least one smell-free suggestion after repair
baseline_name: Pre-repair top-1 suggestion with quality issues
gain_note: Only "up to 80%" of prompts repaired; no pre-repair comparison value given (repair prompts start from flawed suggestions). Mixes security and code smells.
benchmarks: 341 repair prompts per structure (1,023 total) from the above datasets
models: CodeParrot 110M/1.5B; InCoder 1.3B; CodeGen 350M/2B; PolyCoder 160M/0.4B/2.7B; GPT-3.5-Turbo

authors: Mohammed Latif Siddiq; Beatrice Casey; Joanna C. S. Santos
venue: IEEE Working Conference on Source Code Analysis and Manipulation; arXiv

technique_name: Optimo (Mixture-of-Prompts multi-level optimization with differential profiling, mined strategies, correctness reflection)

core_idea_checked: Generated code is checked by Pylint and Bandit, and the structured findings drive repeated LLM repair until issues are resolved.

title: Constrained Decoding for Secure Code Generation
technique_name: Constrained Beam Sampling (positive/negative keyword and template constraints)
core_idea_checked: Beam sampling over code LLMs with manually specified positive and negative keyword/template constraints per prompt, enforcing secure API patterns during decoding.
baseline_name: SVEN prefix tuning with unconstrained decoding (CodeGen-2.7B)
gain_quote: Our results show that constrained decoding over CodeGen (51.25% securepass@1) works better than prefix tuning with unconstrained decoding (36.3% secure-pass@1 for SVEN).
gain_note: Constraints written manually per prompt; same-model beam sampling baseline is 33.77, nucleus 26.07.
effect_correctness_headline: Llama3-8B pass@1 72.21 Constrained Beam vs 82.20 Beam
models: CodeGen-2.7B (open, code); SVEN (CodeGen-2.7B prefix-tuned); StarCoder2-3B; CodeGemma-7B; Llama3-8B; DeepseekCoder-33B; CodeLlama-34B; GPT-4 (closed, baseline only)
note: Constraints are hand-written per prompt, limiting transfer to new benchmarks.
authors: Yanjun Fu; Ethan Baker; Ding, Yu; Chen, Yizheng
venue: arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University); arXiv.org
